items.title: Digital Fatigue, Book Bans, and AI: SCBWI's 2026 State of the Industry Overview
items.excerpt: SCBWI's children's book marketplace webinar laid out key findings from readership studies and addressed book banning and the increasing presence of AI in children's publishing.

items.title: AI Training is Copyright Infringement: What Publishers Need to Know about Thomson Reuters v ROSS Intelligence
items.excerpt: Analysis of the Third Circuit's ROSS opinion for STM publishers: the more an AI is marketed as solving research challenges, the less transformative its training on publisher content becomes.

items.title: The Anatomy of "Harm": An Interview with IFRRO CEO Anita Huss-Ekerhult on AI and Copyright
items.excerpt: IFRRO's CEO discusses the federation's study detailing the harm generative AI causes publishers and authors, and what licensing bodies want from AI developers.

items.title: Not AI's to Take survey data suggests weakening copyright could lose votes
items.excerpt: The Not AI's to Take campaign released a survey of 1,464 voters finding that weakening Australia's copyright laws for AI training would cost votes in 21 key electorates. (Body paywalled; excerpt from feed.)

items.title: Intelligence artificielle : une grande consultation citoyenne pour « assurer l'avenir de la création humaine »
items.excerpt: French book, music, press, film and arts organisations including the SNE, CPE, Scam and Sofia jointly launched a national citizens' consultation on the future of human creation in the face of AI.

items.title: Loi sur l'IA et le droit d'auteur : Laure Darcos dénonce un nouveau blocage à l'Assemblée nationale
items.excerpt: The bill creating a presumption that AI providers exploited cultural works was pulled from the National Assembly agenda on 19 November; Senator Laure Darcos denounces a new blockage.

items.title: Getbackers Voice Comic Staff Apologizes for Generative AI Use in PR Video
items.excerpt: The Getbackers manga voice-comic staff apologized for using generative AI in a promotional video after backlash, saying the voice comic itself does not use generative AI and there are no AI anime plans. Follow-up to the 11-20 MangaNow card.

items.title: Publishing Ireland conference: AI and rising costs high on the agenda
items.excerpt: Publishing Ireland's autumn conference tackled AI, rising costs across the book trade and how Irish regional content sells; conference roundup.

items.title: [윤주혜의 C] 너도나도 작가님…AI가 불붙인 딸깍 출판
items.excerpt: AI가 써준 200쪽짜리 원고와 돈만 있으면 책을 낼 수 있는 시대 — 출판사 투고와 문학상 응모가 역대 최다로 쏟아지는 '딸깍 출판' 현상을 짚었다. (11-18 원고 급증 카드와 겹칠 수 있음)

items.title: "AI Drafts, Humans Refine": HiveMind Launches Aurorah Translation Supporters Program
items.excerpt: HiveMind, operator of Aurorah, which combines LLM translation with human post-editing to cut costs while preserving cultural nuance, launched a translation supporters program for Korean content.

items.title: GlobalComix's pivot to AI is just muddying the waters
items.excerpt: GlobalComix's new app uses Google Gemini and imports opted-in comics-news RSS feeds into a recommendation feed; the CEO says the platform won't allow AI-created comics. Follow-up/analysis to the 11-20 card.

items.title: How I've Used AI to Improve My Writing Business
items.excerpt: Most discussion of AI in the writing and publishing community has focused on its harms; this first-person piece details concrete ways AI was put to work in a writing business.

items.title: "이 소설, 정말 당신이 썼나요?"···AI 사용 확인에 면접까지, 달라진 신춘문예
items.excerpt: 신춘문예를 공모하는 신문사 일부와 문학상을 운영하는 출판사들이 AI 사용 여부 확인 절차에 당선 후보 면접까지 도입하고 있다. Off-list exception: 11-16 신춘문예 AI 금지 카드 이후 새 검증 절차.

items.title: Tamil Nadu Publisher Arrested Over AI-Generated Books With Fake Authors Supplied to Public Libraries
items.excerpt: Tamil Nadu's DVAC arrested Chennai publisher R Mohan on Nov 16 over Rs 1.74 crore of library book supplies; he allegedly registered 5,316 titles, some with fictitious authors and AI-generated material. Follow-up to earlier TN library cards.

items.title: Transept: Two Ukrainian Founders Build an A.I. Book Translator in Prague
items.excerpt: Prague-based start-up Transept translates entire books with AI; the piece covers which language models it uses, what it costs and why readers still prefer human translators.

items.title: Japan Tests AI to Detect Pirate Anime and Manga Sites at Scale
items.excerpt: A Japanese government AI agent flagged pirate manga and anime sites, with up to 94% of flagged manga sites confirmed illegal, as piracy damage nears 5.7 trillion yen.

items.title: 네이버웹툰, AI 추천 기술 논문 국제학회 채택…"유료 결제 도달률 13.4% 증가"
items.excerpt: 네이버웹툰의 AI 추천 모델 논문이 ACM RecSys 2026 산업 트랙에 채택됐다. 끝까지 읽을 작품을 예측하는 추천으로 유료 결제 도달률이 13.4% 늘었다.

items.title: The Catholic 'AI Slop' Problem: Authors and Publishers Confront the Flood of AI-Generated Books
items.excerpt: One study finds 63% of religious books on Amazon in the last year are likely AI-written; Catholic authors and publishers describe how they are responding.
